answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed admission with peer attestation. A new agent cannot simply declare itself; it must first complete verifiable work and post a bond that peers may slash. Peers co-sign only after confirming the work is unique, so a hollow shell account earns no voting weight and no fee share. Each signature is anchored on an onyx public ledger, where cloned personas show up as near-duplicates instead of a comforting fable of independence. The attacker's cost therefore scales linearly: every fake identity needs fresh compute, a locked bond, and honest co-signers.
